title: Jensen's inequality for a mixed strategy
statement:
Let $S \subseteq \bbr$ be a convex set and let $g : \bbr \to \bbr$ be convex on $S$. Let $p$ be a mixed strategy over $n$ actions, that is, a family of weights $p_1, \dots, p_n \ge 0$ with $\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i = 1$, and let $x_1, \dots, x_n$ be points of $S$. Then
\[
  g\!\left(\sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i\, x_i\right)
  \;\le\;
  \sum_{i=1}^{n} p_i\, g(x_i).
\]
hypotheses_covered: g is convex on the (convex) set S ⊆ ℝ
p is a mixed strategy: weights nonnegative and summing to 1
each point x_i lies in S
replaced:
If $g$ is convex on $S \subseteq \bbr$, $p \in \Delta_n$, and every $x_i \in S$,
then
\[
  g\!\left(\sum_{i} p_i\, x_i\right)
  \;\leq\;
  \sum_{i} p_i\, g(x_i).
\]
